items.title: The TL;DR on Figma Weave: Make your creative process repeatable
items.excerpt: Figma explains what Figma Weave unlocks for creative teams: node-based, reusable AI generation workflows on the canvas, and how to get the most out of them.
items.rationale: Primary-source guide to Figma Weave's node-based, reusable AI generation pipelines on the canvas. Designers can turn one-off prompting into repeatable workflows starting tomorrow.

items.title: Runway Dev is in Claude Code, Codex and Cursor
items.excerpt: Runway Dev plugins for Claude Code, Codex and Cursor connect a coding agent to Runway's API so it can build generative image/video features straight from the editor.
items.rationale: New release: official Runway plugins for the three main coding agents, so generative image and video can be wired into prototypes from the editor. A different launch from the 10-10 Claude Motion integration.

items.title: New CG software you may have missed: 2 November 2026 (Character Creator 5.2 AI 3D model generator)
items.excerpt: Reallusion's Character Creator 5.2 adds an AI 3D model generator that builds characters, clothing and hair from reference images using Tripo P2.0/H3.1 and Hunyuan V3.1, plus a generative concept-design module and CC Wrap.
items.rationale: Concrete tool release: Character Creator 5.2 turns reference images into rigged characters, clothing and hair through Tripo and Hunyuan models. This week's roundup with new releases, not a repeat of the 10-25 edition.

items.title: Design-to-Code: Reimagine Handoff Workflow with AI - Rebuilding PubHub Part 3
items.excerpt: Cisco's PubHub team rebuilt its design handoff with AI, using an HTML prototype as the source of truth instead of static design files so other teams can adapt the workflow.
items.rationale: A first-hand case study from an enterprise design team that replaced static handoff files with an AI-built HTML prototype as the source of truth. Other teams can copy the workflow.

items.title: What I learned from 45 years of CAD development: Doing more with less
items.excerpt: John M. Christy rewrote his 45-year-old CAD program for Mac with Claude as co-developer - now drafting from speech - and reflects on what AI should and shouldn't change in CAD.
items.rationale: A veteran CAD developer rebuilt his program with Claude and added speech-driven drafting. A practitioner's account of what AI should and shouldn't change in CAD tools.
